title: The Amazing Roberto Clemente
summary: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant profile Roberto Clemente, the Puerto Rican right fielder for the Pittsburgh Pirates. They cover his five-tool skills and arm, his early life in Carolina, Puerto Rico, and winter ball, the Dodgers signing and the Pirates draft, his experiences with racism in the Jim Crow South and the press, his 1960 World Series and 1971 World Series MVP, his 3,000th hit, and his death in a plane crash on December 31, 1972 while flying relief supplies to earthquake victims in Nicaragua. They also cover his legacy: the Roberto Clemente Award, his Hall of Fame induction, and schools and parks named after him. The episode ends with a listener mail about Eddie Van Halen and a sign-off.

segments.title: Opening banter and career overview
segments.summary: The hosts open with banter about baseball cards, Pirates uniforms and caps, then introduce Roberto Clemente and his career stats, five-tool skills, arm, and humanitarian reputation.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: Mid-episode break before the biography begins.

segments.title: Early life in Carolina, Puerto Rico
segments.summary: Clemente is born in Carolina, Puerto Rico, the youngest of seven, to a sugarcane foreman father and a mother who wanted him to be an engineer. He and friends made their own baseballs and played constantly. The hosts discuss Caribbean baseball development and Puerto Rican winter leagues.

segments.title: Dodgers scouting and Pirates draft
segments.summary: Dodgers scout Al Campanis signs Clemente for about ten thousand dollars under the bonus rule. The Dodgers hide him in the minors, and Branch Rickey brings him to the Pirates in the draft.

segments.title: Racism in the South and the press
segments.summary: Clemente faces Jim Crow segregation during spring training in Fort Myers, Florida, and resents the treatment. The sporting press mocks his English, including a headline spelling hit as heat. His moody reputation and injuries cause criticism.

segments.title: 1960 World Series and return to Puerto Rico
segments.summary: Clemente's breakout in the 1960 World Series with the Pirates, where he was passed over for MVP. He returns to Puerto Rico, buys a house for his mother, mentors kids, and dreams of a sports city. He marries Vera Zabala in 1964.

segments.title: Marine Reserves and family
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Clemente's service in the US Marine Reserves from 1958 and his induction into the Marine Sports Hall of Fame. They also mention his three sons.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: Break before the next segment on his play.

segments.title: Playing style, arm, and fearless play
segments.summary: The hosts describe his fluid build, his unusual running style, his outfield arm, and his javelin background. They also cover his mentorship of other players and his friendship with a Phillies fan named Carol Brezavec.

segments.title: 1966 MVP, 1971 World Series, and 3000 hits
segments.summary: Clemente wins the 1966 National League MVP and goes on to the 1971 World Series against the Orioles, where he hits safely in all seven games and is named MVP. He reaches 3,000 hits in 1972, becoming the first Latin American player to do so.

segments.title: Nicaragua earthquake and fatal 1972 plane crash
segments.summary: After the 1972 season Clemente manages an all-star team in Nicaragua, then organizes relief after the December earthquake. He flies supplies on a DC-7 on December 31, 1972, and the plane crashes into the ocean, killing all five aboard, including him. His body is never recovered.

segments.title: Hall of Fame, awards, and legacy
segments.summary: Clemente is inducted into the Hall of Fame months after his death, the second early induction. The Roberto Clemente Award is created in his honor. Vera Clemente carries on his work and builds the sports city. Dozens of schools, hospitals, and parks bear his name, including a Florida middle school renamed in 2020.

segments.title: Listener mail: Eddie Van Halen
segments.summary: A listener from Melbourne, Matt, writes about watching old Van Halen videos and the timing of Eddie Van Halen's death. The hosts respond and invite emails.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts close the episode and promote the show's email address.
